parts.note: a pair is two of something
to have confronted someone is to have faced them

explanation.surface: A dishonest couple has been challenged face to face.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-faced person shows one face and hides another, which is the essence of being treacherous.

clue.text: Distance from one tip to another of a flier

definitions.text: Distance from one tip to another of a flier

parts.words: Distance from one tip to another of a flier
parts.note: a flier may be a pilot or a leaflet, but here it is a bird or plane measured from end to end of its spread limbs

explanation.surface: A measurement across a bird or aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The measurement across extended wings from one end to the other.

explanation.surface: Archery gear dismissed as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Violin bows are the sticks of a fiddle; the word is also an old exclamation meaning nonsense.

indicators.note: moved signals the remaining letters are rearranged
endless means the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Bravery without limits stirred a big feline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the final E of courage to leave COURAG; 'moved' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The puma or mountain lion of the Americas is a big wild feline.

clue.text: Silly spending day at the back of the ship

parts.words: at the back of the ship
parts.note: aft is the nautical word for the stern area

explanation.surface: A foolish passenger spends a day at the stern.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolish or stupid behaviour is a synonym, informal British usage.

clue.text: Tactful person receives certificate on time

indicators.note: on in a down answer puts the certificate word above the time letter

parts.note: a diploma is a certificate of qualification

explanation.surface: A discreet person is awarded a qualification promptly.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador is skilled in tact, so the word extends to anyone discreet in dealings.

indicators.note: almost means the word falls short by its last letter

parts.note: quite can mean completely, as in quite right

explanation.surface: Surrender very nearly entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon or stop doing something is to cease or desist.

indicators.note: faulty means the letters of the words are wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: Find the defective pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical tube inserted into the body to drain fluid.

clue.text: A small number of animals of a region or all the birds thereof

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals, a small number
fauna is the collective animal life of an area

explanation.surface: A naturalist's definition sentence covering a region's creatures and its birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'or' is a link; 'thereof' points back to the region, so the definition means all the birds of a region.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornithologists use this term for the complete bird population of a given district.

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the word for conclusion surrounds the single letter

parts.note: a conclusion is an end
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: The final chapter concerns an unmarried woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, here standing for any woman, as crosswords often do with names.

clue.text: Time-keeper with an eye on some of the hands?

indicators.note: on places the word for eye after the word for some of the hands in this across answer

parts.note: digits are fingers, so digital relates to some parts of the hands
to eye something is to watch it

explanation.surface: A clock with a pointer on some of its hands, as if keeping an eye on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' suggests clock hands, but here they are human hands whose fingers are digits.
explanation.definitionFit: A wristwatch showing numerals rather than hands is one kind of timepiece.

indicators.note: in places the word for information within the record

parts.note: CD is a compact disc, a record
knowledge is information

explanation.surface: Details recorded on a disc gain credit.
explanation.definitionFit: To be credited or admitted publicly is to be accepted as such.

clue.text: Seemed to have come into view

explanation.surface: Something both looked likely and emerged into sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: something looked a certain way, or something became visible to onlookers.

clue.text: Steer clear of this American city?

explanation.surface: Avoid this town in the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid something is one sense; Dodge City in Kansas is a famous Wild West town.

explanation.surface: Succeed and live through it all.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both to achieve success and to pull through a crisis alive.

indicators.note: back tells us the word for aftertaste is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a tang is a sharp lingering taste

explanation.surface: A vampire left a lingering flavour behind.
explanation.definitionFit: This small biting insect feeds on blood, hence a bloodsucker.

clue.text: One protecting railway worker, a Scotsman

parts.note: a guard works on a train
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A railwayman from Scotland stands as protector.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper or protector watches over someone's welfare.

parts.note: possessed means had, as in owned
it can mean a thing or item, as in a particular object

explanation.surface: An owned object that turns out to be wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' is a link; to have had it is to be done for.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial phrase describes something finished or beyond repair.

parts.note: read 'doubtless' literally: someone without doubt would not pause before acting

explanation.surface: Surely someone wouldn't.
explanation.definitionFit: To pause in uncertainty is something a person free of doubt would not do.

explanation.surface: Done and dusted.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: done and ended, as in 'the game is over' and 'time is up'.

parts.note: discharging sounds like firing an employee, but here the pilot is shot out of the cockpit by a seat mechanism

explanation.surface: A quick method of dismissing an airman.
explanation.definitionFit: Being propelled out of an aircraft is the literal sense, and expulsion generally.

parts.note: a toddler might totter, but a totter is also one who tots up figures, a counting frame

explanation.surface: A small child's wobbly walker.
explanation.definitionFit: This bead-frame device is used for adding up, and children learn to count on it.

parts.note: late means former, ex
a toll is a charge or duty paid
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A night-shift reporter received high praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud someone with enthusiasm is exactly this verb's meaning.

clue.text: Cause another runner to fall when journey has finished

parts.note: a trip is a journey
up means finished, as in time is up

explanation.surface: Bringing down a rival athlete once the trip is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone stumble, literally by catching their foot.

clue.text: Not pleased lady's paid in full

parts.note: Di, short for Diana, is a lady; with the possessive she gives DIS
a debt is satisfied when it is paid in full

explanation.surface: A woman's debts have been fully settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhappy or discontented describes someone left unhappy with an outcome.

indicators.note: from here means made out of the letters of the following word, rearranged

explanation.surface: Drink drawn out of the barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: An old term for a dry white fortified wine from Spain, mentioned by Falstaff.

explanation.surface: Part of a home.
explanation.walkthrough: A SEMI is a British semi-detached house, joined to its neighbour on one side.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefix meaning half, and British slang for a semi-detached house sharing one wall.

clue.text: Way of moving entrance, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the word for entrance is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A manner of travel through the door, as it were.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's walk or stride is their characteristic manner of locomotion.

clue.text: Bill has usual practice to familiarise

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a custom is a usual practice

explanation.surface: An invoice that follows normal procedure helps get people used to things.
explanation.definitionFit: To get someone used to something is to make them familiar with it.

clue.text: I am riding a bicycle without everybody throwing a spanner in the works

definitions.text: throwing a spanner in the works

indicators.note: without means leaving out the word for everybody

parts.note: I'm pedalling is what you would say when riding a bicycle
everybody is all

explanation.surface: A cyclist going it alone causes disruption.
explanation.walkthrough: THROWING A SPANNER IN THE WORKS is a British idiom for sabotaging a process.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstructing or hindering a process is what throwing a spanner does.
